sections.description:
Short title, extent and commencement

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER I
PRELIMINARY
1. Short title, extent and
commencement.‑‑(l) This Ordinance may be
called the Pakistan Postal Services Corporation Ordinance, 1995.
(2) It extends to
the whole of Pakistan.
(3) It shall come
into force at once.

Definitions

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER I
PRELIMINARY
2. Definitions:
‑In this Ordinance unless there is anything repugnant in
the subject or context,‑‑
. (a) "Auditor‑General"
means the Auditor‑General of Pakistan;
(b)
"Board" means the Board of Directors of the Corporation;
(c)
"Chairman" means the Chairman of the Corporation;
(d) "Corporation" means the Pakistan Postal Services
Corporation established under this Ordinance;
(e) "Director" means a Director of the Corporation and includes
Director‑General of the Corporation;
(t) "employees" means employees belonging to the Pakistan Post
Office Department and include employees of the said Department who may, for the
time being, be serving in other organisations but do not include the Chairman,
Directors and members of the Postal Group, other occupational groups or
services or employees of other organisations who may be serving in that said
Department;
(g) "Pakistan Post Office Department" means the Pakistan Post
Office Department set up under the Post Office Act, 1898 (VI of 1898), and
under the control of the Ministry of Communications, Government of Pakistan,
immediately prior to the commencement of this Ordinance;
(h) "Postal Group" means all officers in Basic Pay Scale 17 and
above of the Postal Occupational Group of the Federal Government;
(i) "regulations" means regulations made under section 32;
(j) "rules" means rules made under section 31.

Establishment of corporation

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER II
ESTABLISHMENT OF THE CORPORATION AND SHARE
CAPITAL
3. Establishment of the Corporation.‑‑‑(1) As from the
commencement of this Ordinance, there shall be established for carrying out the
purposes of this Ordinance a Corporation to be known as the Pakistan Postal
Services Corporation or, in brief, as Pakistan Post.
(2) The Corporation shall be a body corporate having perpetual succession
and a common seal, with power to acquire, hold and dispose of property and
shall by the name specified in subsection (1) sue and be sued.

Share capital and its issue

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER II
ESTABLISHMENT OF THE CORPORATION AND SHARE
CAPITAL
4. Share capital and its issue: ‑‑(1) The authorized share
capital of the Corporation shall, in the first instance, be two billion rupees
only divided into two hundred million shares of ten rupees each, but it may be
increased by the Federal Government from time to time.
(2) The subscribed and paid‑up capital
of the Corporation shall, in the first instance, be seven hundred sixty‑four
million rupees divided into seventy six million and four hundred thousand
shares of ten rupees each.
(3) The initial allotment of shares shall be
made to the Federal Government out of the net‑worth of the Pakistan Post
Office certified by the Auditor‑General, being the excess of historic
cost less depreciation of the $‑iced assets plus other assets over the
liabilities vested in the Corporation under section 6, in such sum as the
Federal Government may desire.
(4) The Federal ‑ Government may at any
time authorize the Corporation to increase the subscribed and paid‑up
capital to be allotted to the Federal Government or the general public.

Transfer of departmental employees

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER III
EXISTING ARRANGEMENTS
5. Transfer of departmental employees: ‑‑(1) Notwithstanding
anything contained in any law, contract or agreement, or in the conditions of
service, on the establishment of the Coloration, all employees of Pakistan Post
Office Department shall, subject to subsection (1) of section 34, stand
transferred to, and become employees of, the Corporation on the same terms and
conditions to which they were entitled
immediately before such transfer, provided that the Corporation shall be
competent to take disciplinary action against any. such employee.
(2) The terms and conditions of service of any such person as is referred
to in subsection (1) shall not be varied by the Corporation to his
disadvantage.
(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in
force, no person who stands transferred to the Corporation under subsection (1)
shall be entitled to any compensation because of such transfer.

Transfer of assets and liabilities

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER III
EXISTING ARRANGEMENTS
6. Transfer of assets and liabilities.‑(1) As from the commencement
of this Ordinance, all properties and assets including installations and
plants, bank accounts, deposits, securities and rights vested in the Pakistan
Post Office Department, including the balance of Postal Life Insurance Fund and
the amount of Savings Bank deposits standing to the credit of Savings Bank
depositors, holders of Savings Certificates shall vest in the Corporation and
all liabilities of the Pakistan Post Office Department in respect of the said
assets shall be the liability of the Corporation:
Provided that‑‑‑
(a) the total liability in respect of the accumulated capital and the
amount of interest on such assets and property shall be considered as paid off
from the date of effect of this Ordinance; and "
(b) the total pensionary charges payable before the commencement of this
Ordinance shall cease to be the liability of the Corporation.
Explanation.‑For the purpose of this subsection,
"installations and plants" include buildings, land, interests in
land, machinery, apparatus, equipment, computers, stores, vehicles and other
appliances or accessories used for, or in connection with postal and other
services of the Pakistan Post Office Department.
(2) All contracts and working arrangements made and all liabilities
incurred by the Pakistan Post Office Department before the commencement of this
Ordinance shall be deemed to be made or incurred by the Corporation and shall
be enforceable accordingly.

Related organization

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER III
EXISTING ARRANGEMENTS
7. Related organisations.‑‑‑As from the commencement of
this Ordinance, all organisations, including Pakistan Postal Life Insurance,
Post Office Savings Bank and Special Mail Services, related to, or forming part
of, the Pakistan Post Office Department shall form part of the Corporation.

Head office branches etc.

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER IV
MANAGEMENT
8. Head
office, branches, etc.‑‑‑(1) The Head Office of the
Corporation
shall be at
Islamabad.
(2) All other offices, heretofore offices of the Pakistan Post Office
Department shall continue to function in the name of the Corporation.
(3) The Corporation may, with the approval of the Federal Government, set
up branches elsewhere in Pakistan and abroad.

Administration of the affairs of the corporation

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER IV
MANAGEMENT
9. Administration of the affairs of the
Corporation.‑‑(I) The general direction and the administration of
the Corporation and its affairs shall vest in the Board which may exercise all
powers and do all acts which may be exercised or done by the Corporation.
(2) The Federal Government may, as and when it considers necessary, issue
directives to the Corporation and such directives shall be binding on the
Corporation.

The board

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER IV
MANAGEMENT
10. The Board: ‑‑(1) The Board shall consist of the following
Directors to be appointed by the Federal Government, namely;‑‑
(a) the Chairman;
and
(b) not more than thirteen other Directors including Secretaries incharge
of Ministries of Communications, Finance, Planning and Development and at least
three full‑time Directors‑General of the Corporation drawn from the
Postal Occupational Group, Director‑General (Finance) and Director‑General
(Administration) of the Corporation.
(2) If and when any shares of the Corporation are to be issued to the
private sector, the Federal Government shall determine the number of Directors
to be elected to represent the private shareholders and specify the procedure
for their election:
Provided that the aggregate number of Directors appointed under
subsection (1) and those elected under this subsection shall not exceed
thirteen.
(3) Each Director shall‑‑‑
(a) perform any specific duties as the Board may,. by regulations, assign
to him; and
(b) receive such remuneration, fees or allowances as the Federal
Government may determine.

Chairman

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER IV
MANAGEMENT
11. Chairman.‑‑‑(1) The
Chairman shall be a whole‑time officer and the
Chief Executive of
the Corporation and shall hold office for a term of three years and generally
be appointed from amongst the senior officers of the Corporation or of the
Postal Group on such terms and conditions as the Federal Government may
determine.
(2) Any person ceasing to be Chairman by reason of expiry of the term of
his office shall be eligible for re‑appointment for another term or for
such shorter term as the Federal Government may decide.
(3) The Chairman may at any time resign his office, but his resignation
shall not take effect until it has been accepted by the Federal Government.

Term of office of director

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER IV
MANAGEMENT
12. Term of office of Director: ‑‑A Director shall hold
office for a term of three years and, subject to the provisions of this
Ordinance, be eligible for re appointment.

Removal of chairman and directors-general

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER IV
MANAGEMENT
13. Removal of Chairman and Directors‑General: ‑‑The
Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, remove the
Chairman or any Director‑General if he refuses or fails to discharge or
becomes, in the opinion of the Federal Government, incapable of discharging his
responsibilities under this Ordinance.

Delegation of power

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER IV
MANAGEMENT
14. Delegation of power.‑‑‑The Board may, from time to
time, delegate any of its powers to the Chairman, any committee constituted by
it, or any officer of the Corporation, subject to such conditions . as the
Board may determine.

Disqualification of director

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER IV
MANAGEMENT
15, Disqualification of Director.‑‑‑(1) No person shall
be appointed or shall continue to be a Director who‑‑‑
(a) is, or at any time has been, convicted‑. of an offence
involving moral turpitude; or
(b) is, or at any time has been,
adjudicated insolvent; or
(c) is lunatic or becomes of
unsound mind; or
(d) is a minor.
(2) No Director shall continue in office after absenting himself from
three consecutive meetings of the Board without the leave of the Chairman or,
in the case of the Chairrnar.. ,it ih,,; Federal Government.

Chairman, director and other employees to be public servants

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER IV
MANAGEMENT
16. Chairman. Directors and other employees to he public servants: ‑‑(1)
fhe Chairman. Directors, Officera, cnrplurees uid servants of the Corporation
shall, when acting or purporting to act in pursuance of any of the provisions
of this Ordinance., be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of
section 21 of the Pakistan Perr.,l (.odr (Aer XL.V of 1860):
(2) No suit, prosecution or legal proceedings
shall lie against the Corporation, the Chairman, the Directors, Officers,
employees and servants of the Corporation, in respect of anything done or
intended to be done in good faith under this Ordinance.

Meetings of the board

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER IV
MANAGEMENT
17. Meetings of the Board: ‑‑(1)
There shall be at least one meeting of the Board in each quarter of a year.
(2) The meetings of the Board shall be held
at such time and at such places as may be prescribed by regulations or, until
regulations are made in this behalf, as and when convened by the Chairman.
(3) Notwithstanding the provisions of subsections (1) and (2), the Chairman
shall convene a meeting of the Board if three or more Directors so request him
in writing.
(4) To constitute a quorum at a meeting of the Board, the Chairman and
five other Directors shall be present.
(5) The Chairman or, in his absence, a Director elected by the Board for
the purpose shall preside, at the meetings of the Board:
(6) Each Director including the Chairman shall have one vote and in the
event of an equality of votes the Chairman shall have a casting vote.
(7) No act or proceedings of the Board shall be invalid merely on the
ground of the existence of any vacancy in, or any defect in the constitution
of, the Board.

Executive committee

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER IV
MANAGEMENT
18. Executive Committee: ‑‑(1) There shall be an Executive
Committee of the Board consisting of the following members, namely:‑‑
(a) the Chairman;
and
(b) three
Directors to be elected,by the Board.
(2) A member of the Executive Committee shall hold office for three years
or till the expiry of tenure of his office as Director, whichever is earlier.
(3) Subject to the regulations made in this behalf and such general or
special directions as may, from time to time, be given by the Board, the
Executive Committee shall deal with any matter within the competence of the
Board.
(4) The minutes of every meeting of the Executive Committee shall be laid
before the Board at its meeting following the meeting of the. Executive
Committee.

Advisory committees

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER IV
MANAGEMENT
19. Advisory Committees: ‑‑(1) The Corporation may appoint an
Advisory Committee or Committees as it thinks fit to assist in the efficient
discharge of its functions.
(2) The Advisory Committee shall advise the
Board on such matters as may be referred to it.
(3) The meetings of the Advisory Committee shall be convened by the
Chairman at such time and at such places as he may deem necessary.
(4) The members of the Advisory Committee
shall be paid such fees and travel costs for attending the meetings as may be
prescribed by regulations.

Purposes and functions of the corporation

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER V
FUNCTIONS OF THE CORPORATION
20. Purposes and Functions of the
Corporation: ‑‑(1) The purposes and functions of the Corporation
shall be‑‑‑
(a) to establish, maintain and operate postal services throughout the
country and between Pakistan and other countries;
(b) to operate such other postal communications, banking or insurance
services as may be assigned to it, from time to time, by the Federal Government
and the Provincial Governments according to mutually agreed arrangements and to
plan, promote, organise and implement programmes for the provision of such
services in all parts of Pakistan, including cities, towns and villages,
territorial waters of Pakistan. ships,
aircrafts and spacecrafts';
(c) to establish, maintain and operate Post Office Savings Banks
throughout the country;
(d) to establish, maintain and operate Postal Life Insurance Service
throughout the country;
(e) to make such provisions as appears to it to be appropriate for
advancing the skills of its officers, employees and servants by education,
training and otherwise, and to promote, within reasonable limits, their
welfare;
(f) to conduct and assist research, experiments or trials for the
improvement of methods of postal facilities and other services being carried on
by the Corporation;
(g) to advise Government on matters relating to postal and other services
being provided by the Corporation and to provide consultancy services thereto;
(h) to regulate the operation of private couriers.in order to safeguard
the interest of the State and the public; ,
(i) to maintain liaison with Universal Postal Union and other
international postal organisations;
(j) to open, operate and maintain
bank accounts;
(k) to borrow domestic or foreign funds on such terms and conditions as
may be approved by the Board; .
(1). to seek contracts and provide
postal services abroad;
(m) to invest the funds of the Corporation in such manner as the Board
may deem fit; and
(n) to perform any other function which is supplemental, incidental or
consequential to any of the purposes and functions aforesaid.
(2) Subject to such conditions as the Federal Government may impose, from
time to time, the Corporation shall be deemed to enjoy the exclusive privilege
of the Federal Government within the meaning of section 4 of the Post Office
Act, 1898 (VI of 1898).
(3) Without prejudice to any provision of this Ordinance any power,
privilege or concession granted to the Pakistan Post Office Department shall,
mutatis mutandis, be deemed to have been granted to the Corporation.
(4) In performing its functions, the
Corporation shall have due regard to the‑‑‑
(a) desirability of improving and
developing its operating system;
(b) technological developments in the field
of postal and other services being carried on by it;
(c) efficiency and economy; and
(d) commercial viability and social
benefits. .
(5) The Corporation may take such measures
and exercise such powers as it may consider necessary or expedient for carrying
out. the purposes of this Ordinance, and these may include establishing
subsidiary companies for operating and developing postal facilities and other
services being carried on by the Corporation.
(6) Nothing in the preceding subsections
shall be taken to preclude the Corporation for justifiable reasons from
interrupting, suspending or restricting postal and other services provided by
it, or be construed as imposing upon the
Corporation, either
directly or indirectly, any form of duty or liability enforceable by
proceedings before any Court.

Plans and schemes

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER V
FUNCTIONS OF THE CORPORATION
21. Plans and schemes: ‑‑(1) The
Corporation shall from time to time P~ prepare for the approval of the Federal
Government, plans and, if necessary, perspective plans, for the development of
postal and other services and for the furtherance of its purposes and functions
under this Ordinance, and matters incidental thereto.
(2) The Corporation may frame a scheme or schemes for all or any of the
following matters, namely:‑‑
(a) expansion and development of the Corporation's postal facilities and
other services in urban and rural areas;
(b) introduction of new services‑ to meet the needs of the changing
times;
(c) research and development in the
postal field;
(d) replacement and creation of
assets;
(e) improvements in the quality and
grade of postal and other services;
(f) training of the Corporation's
employees;
(g) promotion and establishment of facilities in Pakistan for the
betterment of postal and other services;
(h) welfare of the Corporation's
employees; and
(i) any other matter pertaining
to the purposes and functions of the Corporation or incidental thereto.
(3) The Board may finally approve any scheme prepared under subsection
(2), provided the scheme is covered by an overall plan approved by the Federal
GoVernment.

Federal Government postal investment funds account

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER VI
FINANCE, AUDITANDACCOUNTS
22. Federal Government Postal Investment Fund Account‑‑‑The
balance of the "net‑worth" after initial allotment of shares
under section 4 shall be transferred to a loan account to be named
"Federal Government Postal Investment Fund Account" which shall bear
a mark‑up of seven per cent. per annum payable to the Federal Government.

Liability of federal Government to be limited

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER VI
FINANCE, AUDITANDACCOUNTS
23. Liability of Federal Government to be
limited: ‑‑The liability of the Federal Government to the creditors
of the Corporation shall be limited to the extent of grants made by the Federal
Government and the loans raised by the Corporation with the sanction of the
Federal Government.

Postal tariffs

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER VI
FINANCE, AUDITANDACCOUNTS
24. Postal tariffs: ‑‑(1) Rates of
postage to be charged in respect of ordinary postal articles sent by the inland
post shall, notwithstanding anything contained in the Post Office Act, 1898 (VI
of 1898), be fixed by the Corporation with the prior approval of the Federal
Government:
Provided that the rates being charged by the Pakistan Post Office Department
immediately before the commencement of this Ordinance shall be deemed to have
been approved by the Federal Government.
(2) Rates of postage to be charged in respect of postal articles sent
abroad shall be fixed by the Federal Government according to the relevant
provisions of the Convention adopted by the latest Congress of the Universal
Postal Union or in accordance with its international obligations.
(3) Fees to be charged in respect of postal articles requiring special
treatment and for remittance of money shall be fixed by the Corporation.
(4) In fixing the tariffs as aforesaid, the Board
shall take into account the cost of providing services and the need to mobilize
funds for the development of postal services and to earn a reasonable return on
the investment. ,
(5) The Board may, from time to time, settle with foreign postal
authorities rates at which accounts are to be settled with such authorities in
respect of postal traffic between Pakistan and other countries.
(6) In the case of any conflict between tariffs
determined under subsection (1), from time to time, and the rules made under
the Post Office Act, 1898 (VI of 1898), the said rules shall, on and from the
date of determination of tariffs under that subsection, stand amended to the extent
necessary to remove such conflict.

Rates of profit and bonus

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER VI
FINANCE, AUDITANDACCOUNTS
25. Rates of profit and bonus: ‑‑(1) Rates of profit payable
to depositors and investors of the savings schemes operated by the Corporation
shall be determined by the Federal Government.
(2) Rates of bonus payable on postal life
insurance policies shall be fixed by the Corporation on the advice of the
actuary conducting the valuation of the postal life insurance fund.

Annual budget

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER VI
FINANCE, AUDITANDACCOUNTS
26. Annual budget: ‑‑(1) The annual
budget of the Corporation shall be approved by the Board and any deficit
therein shall, during the first five years, be met by a grant from the Federal
Government.
(2) The budgetary deficits, if any, after the first five years shall be
met by the Corporation itself, either by raising interest bearing loans or by
rent or sale of its assets.
(3) The Board may, within the budgetary allocations, authorise any
expenditure
considered necessary for the efficient performance of the functions of the
Corporation, including re‑appropriation from one head of account to
another.
(4) The surplus revenue, if any, shall be utilized by the Corporation for
its development projects.

Exemption from taxes

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER VI
FINANCE, AUDITANDACCOUNTS
27. Exemption from taxes: ‑‑(1) Notwithstanding anything
contained in the Income Tax Ordinance, 1979
(XXXI of 1979), the Wealth Tax Act, 1963 (XV of 1963), or any other law for
the time being in force relating to income tax, super‑tax or wealth‑tax,
the Corporation shall not be liable to pay such tax on its income, profits or
gains for the first five years.
(2) All goods imported by, or on
behalf of, the Corporation shall be exempt from customs duty and sales tax for
the first five years.

Audit and account

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER VI
FINANCE, AUDITANDACCOUNTS
28. Audit and accounts: ‑‑(1) The Corporation shall maintain
proper accounts and other relevant records to reflect true and fair view of its
state of affairs and prepare annual statements of accounts; including the
profit and loss account and balance‑sheet.
(2) The accounts of the Corporation shall be audited by an auditor or
auditors who shall be Chartered Accountants within the meaning of the Chartered
Accountants Ordinance, 1961 (XII of
1961), to be appointed by the Board, with the prior approval of the Federal
Government.
(3) Notwithstanding the audit provided for in subsection (2), the Auditor‑General
shall have the power to audit or cause to be audited the accounts of the
Corporation.
(4) The Corporation shall produce such accounts and books and connected
documents, and furnish such explanations and information, as the Auditor‑General,
or any officer authorized by him in this behalf, may require for the purpose of
the audit.
(5) Copies of the audit report shall be sent to the Corporation and to
the Federal Government, and shall also be available for public inspection.
(6) The Corporation shall comply with any directive issued by the Federal
Government or the Public Accounts Committee of the National Assembly for the
rectification of an audit objection.

Internal audit

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER VI
FINANCE, AUDITANDACCOUNTS
29. Internal Audit.‑‑‑The Corporation shall, in
addition to the audit under section 28, cause to be carried out internal audit
of its accounts and submit the reports to the Board through the Chairman.

Reports and return

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER VI
FINANCE, AUDITANDACCOUNTS
30. Reports and returns.‑‑‑(1) As soon as possible
after the end of every financial year, but before the last day of December next
falling, the Corporation shall submit to the Federal Government a report on the
conduct of its affairs for that year.
(2) The Federal Government shall cause to be laid before the National
Assembly and the Senate a copy of the report referred to in subsection (1)
together with a copy of the audit report referred to in section 28.
(3) The Corporation shall brief the Committees of the Senate and the
National Assembly about its activities and future plans as and when so required
by such Committees.
(4) The Federal Government may require the Corporation to furnish it with‑‑‑
(a) any return, statement, estimate, statistics or other information or
report regarding any matter under the control of the Corporation; and
(b) a copy of any document in the charge of the Corporation; and the
Corporation shall comply with every such requisition.

Power to make rules

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES
CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER VII
RULES AND REGULATIONS
31. Power to make rules: ‑‑(1) The Federal Government may
make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Ordinance and where the
regulations made under section 32 are inconsistent with the rules made under
this section, the rules shall prevail.
(2) In particular and without prejudice to the generality of the
foregoing powers, such rules may provide for‑‑‑
(a) the manner in which and the conditions subject to which the shares of
the Corporation may be held and transferred and generally all matters relating
to the rights and duties of the shareholders;
(b) the duties and powers of the
Chairman;
(c) the maintenance of liaison and coordination between the Corporation
and its Divisions, offices and authorities concerned with administration and
development;
(d) organisation of training schemes for the officers and employees of
the Corporation;
(e) the determination of the terms and conditions of service of the
officers and employees of the Corporation; and
(f) the constitution and management
of provident fund and welfare
fund for the
officers, employees and servants of the Corporation and all matters connected
with such funds.
(3) Till such time the rules are made under subsection (1), the rules
applicable to the Pakistan Post Office Department, including those for
appointment, recruitment; promotion and transfer shall continue to remain in
force.

Power to make regulations

ORDINANCE XXVIII
ORDINANCE XXVIII .OF 1995
PAKISTAN POSTAL SERVICES CORPORATION ORDINANCE, 1995
CHAPTER VII
RULES AND REGULATIONS
32. Power to make regulation: ‑‑(1) The Board may, with the
approval of the Federal Government, make regulations not inconsistent with this
Ordinance or the rules to provide for giving effect to the provisions of this
Ordinance and the efficient conduct of the affairs of the Corporation.
(2) In particular and without
prejudice to the generality of the foregoing powers, such regulations may
provide for‑‑‑
(a) the appointment of committees,
their functions and powers;
(b) the investment of moneys by the‑
Corporation;

33. Publication of rules and regulations. All rules and regulations made
under this Ordinance shall be published in the Official Gazette and shall come
into force upon such publication.

Appointment of officers, advisors and servants

34. Appointment of officers, advisors and servants‑‑(I) The
corpration may, from time to time, appoint in accordance with rules, such officers and servants as it may consider
necessary for the performance of its functions:
Provided that the Corporation may appoint
advisors, consultants arid experts on such terms and conditions as it may deem
fit:
Provided further that all officers of the
Postal Group serving in the Pakistan Post Office Departmgnt or in any other
organisation on, the commencement of this Ordinance and all officers of the
Postal Group recruited after such commencement shall stand transferred on
permanent basis to, and serve in, the Corporation on such terms and conditions
as the Federal Government may, in consultation with the Corporation, determine
but shall not be entitled to. any deputation allowance:
Provided further that where the Federal
Government so desires any officer of the Postal Group may be withdrawn from the
service of the Corporation and posted elsewhere in accordance with the
provisions of Civil Servants Act, 1973 (LXXI of 1973):
Provided also that the Federal Government
may, in relation to any such officer, delegate such administrative,
disciplinary and financial powers to the Corporation as the Federal Government
may deem tit.
(2) Subject to the rules, the Corporation
shall be competent to take disciplinary action against its officers and other
employees.
(3) Service under the Corporation is declared
to be service of Pakistan and every person holding a post under the
Corporation, not being a person who is on deputation to the Corporation, shall
be deemed to be a civil servant for the purposes of the Service Tribunals Act,
1973 (LXX of 1973).

into joint ventures for operation or expansion of its services or functions and
may sell its assets and services.

acquisition of any land or any interest in
land for the Corporation for any scheme under this Ordinance, or for the
establishment, maintenance and working of post offices or other offices
of the
Corporation, or for matters directly connected therewith, shall be deemed

37. Recovery of sums due to the Corporation: ‑‑Any sum
payable to the Corporation in respect of any postal or other services rendered
by the Corporation shall, in addition to any other mode prescribed by law or
rules, be recoverable as an arrear of land revenue.

relating to winding up of companies shad apply to the Corporation and the
Corporation shall not be wound up save by order of the Federal Government and
in such manner as the Federal Government may direct.

entering upon his office make, declaration of fidelity and secrecy in the form
set out in the Schedule to this Ordinance.

Government may make such order, not inconsistent with the provisions of this

41. Savings.‑Nothing in this Ordinance shall derogate from or
affect the provisions of the Post Office Act, 1898 (VI of 1898), the Government
Savings Bank Act, 1873 (V of 1873), the Post Office
Cash Certificates Act, 1917 (XVIII of 1917), the Post Office National Savings
Certificates Ordinance, 1944 (XLII of 15144),

or extending the same, provided that reference to the Pakistan Post Office therein shall hereafter be read and construed
